title: Exceptional internal-Hom exchange preserves the mate of an open-restricted morphism
statement:
Fix the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $A=A_{E,n}$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Work in the finite-Tor constructible categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$ with the canonical ordinary and exceptional adjunctions and composition comparisons of [def-trf-admissibility]. Let $C$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $j:W\hookrightarrow C$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(C,A)$ and $f:M\to N$. Write $H=R\mathcal Hom_A(M,N)$, $H_W=R\mathcal Hom_A(Lj^*M,Rj^!N)$ using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $\widetilde f:A_C\to H$ be the tensor–Hom transpose of $f$. Use the normalized open-purity comparison $Lj^*\simeq Rj^!$ of [prop-functor-package] to regard $Lj^*f$ as $f_W:Lj^*M\to Rj^!N$; let $\widetilde f_W:A_W\to H_W$ be its tensor–Hom transpose. Let $E_j:H_W\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!H$ be the canonical exceptional internal-Hom exchange of [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange] and $a:A_W\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj^!A_C$ the constant-pullback comparison followed by open purity. Then
$$E_j\circ\widetilde f_W=Rj^!(\widetilde f)\circ a.$$
All the comparisons in this equality are the specified ones, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms of the displayed objects.

source.place: §0.3(a)-(b), equation (0.3): section normalization of exceptional internal-Hom exchange.

proof.text: Transport along the normalized open-purity comparison in [prop-functor-package](6). By [prop-exc-open-adjoint] we may compute with $J=j_!$ and $R=Lj^*=Rj^!$, with the same adjunction $J\dashv R$, unit $u$ and counit $e$; in particular the exceptional counit becomes $e$. Write $\mathbf1=A_C$, $\mathbf1'=A_W$ and $a:\mathbf1'\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathbf1$ for the constant-pullback map. Then $f_W=Rf$. All calculations may be made in the ordinary ambient derived module categories, where the open adjunction is unconditional, and hence also hold between the given objects of their full finite-Tor constructible subcategories. The tensor-Hom adjunction, including its naturality and evaluation, is clause (i) of [sk-def-sf-operations]. Suppress only the canonical tensor unitors and restriction/tensor identifications.

source.place: §0.3(a); normalized open adjunction and tensor-Hom conventions

proof.text:
We first compute the exceptional tensor map $T_j(B,D):RB\otimes RD\to R(B\otimes D)$ for $B=H$, $D=M$. In [def-exchange-projection] choose the compactification of $j$ with proper factor the identity. The identity factor has identity unit and counit, so its projection map is the identity. Thus the open projection map is $\gamma_{P,D}:JP\otimes D\xrightarrow{\sim}J(P\otimes RD)$. The statement of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] specifies its inverse by
$$R(\gamma_{P,D}^{-1})\circ u_{P\otimes RD}=u_P\otimes1_{RD}$$
under the restriction/tensor identification. The definition of $T_j$ is the $J\dashv R$ transpose of $(e_B\otimes1_D)\circ\gamma_{RB,D}^{-1}$. Its transpose is therefore
$$R(e_B\otimes1_D)\circ R(\gamma_{RB,D}^{-1})\circ u_{RB\otimes RD}=(R(e_B)\circ u_{RB})\otimes1_{RD}=1_{RB}\otimes1_{RD}.$$
The last equality is the triangle identity. Thus $T_j(B,D)$ is exactly the canonical restriction/tensor comparison $RB\otimes RD\xrightarrow{\sim}R(B\otimes D)$, rather than that comparison followed by an automorphism. This is a direct substitution into the cited inverse-projection unit equation.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; open-unit refinement in lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, and Varshavsky §0.3(b), equation (0.2)

proof.text:
Let $Q=E_j^{-1}:RH\to H_W$. The word canonical in [lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange] refers to the evaluation-defined exchange: in the inverse direction displayed in Varshavsky (0.3), $Q$ is the tensor-Hom transpose of
$$RH\otimes RM\xrightarrow{T_j(H,M)}R(H\otimes M)\xrightarrow{R(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})}RN.$$
Here $T_j$ uses the inverse projection map and exceptional counit, exactly as computed in Step 2; the open projection is the one defined in [def-exchange-projection]. Consequently, writing $\mu_{H,M}:RH\otimes RM\xrightarrow{\sim}R(H\otimes M)$ for that restriction/tensor comparison, its defining evaluation equation is
$$\mathrm{ev}_{RM,RN}\circ(Q\otimes1_{RM})=R(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})\circ\mu_{H,M}.$$
This unpacks the specified canonical map; it does not select an arbitrary isomorphism between the two objects.

source.place: §0.3(b), equations (0.2)-(0.3): definition by projection, exceptional counit and evaluation

proof.text:
Apply the tensor-Hom bijection to the map $Q\circ R(\widetilde f)\circ a:\mathbf1'\to H_W$. Step 3 and the naturality in both factors of the derived tensor/pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] give its uncurried map as
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{ev}_{RM,RN}\circ((Q\circ R\widetilde f\circ a)\otimes1_{RM})
&=R(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N})\circ\mu_{H,M}\circ(R\widetilde f\otimes1_{RM})\circ(a\otimes1_{RM})\\
&=R\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_{M,N}\circ(\widetilde f\otimes1_M)\bigr)\circ\mu_{\mathbf1,M}\circ(a\otimes1_{RM})\\
&=Rf.
\end{aligned}$$
In the last line $\mathrm{ev}_{M,N}\circ(\widetilde f\otimes1_M)=f$ under $\mathbf1\otimes M=M$, by the tensor-Hom transpose definition. Also $\mu_{\mathbf1,M}\circ(a\otimes1)$ is the canonical unitor identification $\mathbf1'\otimes RM\cong RM$: restriction of the coefficient unit is the coefficient unit and $a$ is precisely that unit map. On a K-flat representative for $M$, this composite is the chain map $1\otimes m\mapsto m$ in every degree, so the unitor equality holds in the derived category. The comparison and its naturality are those in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Since $\widetilde f_W$ is the transpose of $f_W=Rf$, injectivity of the tensor-Hom bijection [sk-def-sf-operations](i) gives $Q\circ R\widetilde f\circ a=\widetilde f_W$. Postcompose with $E_j=Q^{-1}$ and restore the normalized open-purity identifications. This gives the required equality with the specified maps.

source.place: §0.3(a)-(b), equation (0.3): explicit naturality and transposition calculation

proof_origin.place: §0.3(a)-(b), equations (0.2)-(0.3); explicit open-unit normalization and transpose calculation
